sections.title: Executive investment summary: a two-year-old EPC business in a 30-year-old enclosure company, priced for distress

blocks.text: RMC Switchgears makes plastic, fibre-reinforced-plastic and sheet-metal hardware for India's power distribution network. The range covers smart-meter enclosures, feeder pillars, distribution and junction boxes, FRP safety products, LT panels and bus bars, all made at one plant at Chaksu near Jaipur [F] (AR2026 p.6). Since FY2025 most revenue has come from turnkey projects rather than hardware: distribution and transmission EPC, and solar EPC (ground-mounted, rooftop and pumps) [F] (AR2026 p.27). It makes money in two ways: short-cycle product supply (about three months) and project contracts billed over roughly one year (solar) or two years (electrical EPC) [MC] (AR2026 p.14).

items: End markets: government and utility work. Solar EPC and electrical EPC are all government; about 30% of Electrical Products is government and 70% B2B. The CEO put B2B at only '10% or 5%' of total revenue [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

Geography: 100% of standalone FY26 revenue was booked in India and nothing outside India, against Rs 0.89 cr of exports in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.56). A state-wise split is not disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.84).

Customer profile: state DISCOMs and transcos (MSEDCL since 2004, the Rajasthan Vidyut Vitran Nigams since 2003), generation companies, meter makers and EPC contractors [F] (AR2026 p.13). Revenue by customer and concentration ratios are not disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.84).

Listing: the stock moved from the BSE SME platform (listed 2017) to the BSE Main Board and NSE on 1 April 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.3). Quarterly reporting therefore starts only in FY26. The Q3 and Q4 FY26 numbers were certified by management, not audited [F] (AR2026 p.44). Corporate-governance provisions applied only from the migration date [F] (AR2026 p.36). Our evidence base is thin: one Main Board annual report, two management calls, one deck and no prospectus. A prospectus or placement document was not available to us [AI].

blocks.text: **The hardware business is not what drives today's numbers.** FY26 revenue of Rs 401.59 cr came 52% from a solar EPC vertical that earned Rs 1.74 cr in FY25 and runs through subsidiaries set up in July-September 2024 [F] (AR2026 p.27; AR2026 p.31). Electrical Products and Electrical EPC together fell from Rs 314.56 cr to Rs 192.61 cr, down 38.8% [E] (AR2026 p.27).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. Profits do not turn into cash. Operating cash flow was 0.12x reported profit over three years and free cash flow was Rs -34 cr in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Consolidated CFO was Rs -11.60 cr while PAT was Rs 22.42 cr [F] (AR2026 p.68).

2. Receivables are ageing, and the ageing contradicts management. 67% of the Rs 205.18 cr of consolidated receivables were more than six months past due at March 2026 [E] (AR2026 p.73). The CEO said only '3% to 5%' was above six months, excluding retention [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The two are not reconciled.

3. Credit ratings show distress or non-transparency. CARE reaffirmed 'CARE D' under issuer-not-cooperating on 12 Nov 2025. Brickwork reaffirmed 'BWR D' (INC) and withdrew the rating on 10 Apr 2026 at the company's request [F] (RATING). The directors' report says there was no default [MC] (AR2026 p.34), and a post-year-end Infomerics 'IVR BBB; Stable' rating is cited [MC] (AR2026 p.31). These are not reconciled.

4. Group sales flatter the standalone entity. The parent sold Rs 105.99 cr of goods to its subsidiary RMC Solar Park and Rs 6.38 cr is outstanding from it [F] (AR2026 p.61). About 36.5% of standalone revenue was intra-group [E] (AR2026 p.61; AR2026 p.45).

5. Funding is getting more expensive and more opaque. Short-term borrowings rose to Rs 89.38 cr [F] (AR2026 p.9). From December 2025 the company took unsecured NBFC and bank loans at 13.75-15% fixed [F] (AR2026 p.54). It also carries Rs 56.09 cr of supplier-financing payables outside reported borrowings [F] (AR2026 p.55).

6. A rights issue is imminent at a depressed price. The board meets on 9 Oct 2026 to consider it, and authorised capital was raised from Rs 15 cr to Rs 20 cr [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). In November 2025 management had called equity at those market conditions 'value destructive' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).

7. Governance lapses are documented. The secretarial auditor recorded an unreported promoter contra trade, late Reg 30 disclosures and SDD lapses [F] (AR2026 p.35), plus a Rs 44,000 BSE fine for a late FY24 annual report [F] (AR2026 p.39). The CFO role has been held by a promoter-family whole-time director since July 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.22).

8. Related-party exposure is large relative to the balance sheet. Shareholders approved loans and guarantees to subsidiaries of up to Rs 485 cr [E] (AR2026 p.89), against Rs 130.64 cr of consolidated equity [F] (AR2026 p.67). Loans to RMC Green Energy are at 9.2% [F] (AR2026 p.97) while the parent borrows at up to 15% [F] (AR2026 p.54).

9. Execution has repeatedly lagged what management said. The Nov 2025 order pipeline of about Rs 825 cr was 'to be delivered over the next 12 months' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Seven months later the book was still 'Rs 850 crore plus' and EPC was described as taking two years [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Q1 FY27 revenue fell 55.95% YoY [F] (PPT Sep 2026).

10. The headline growth started from a collapse. FY19 sales were Rs 132 cr [F] (NUMBERS) and FY22 revenue was Rs 41.6 cr [F] (AR2026 p.7). The '10x in four years' narrative [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) measures from a trough. FY19 to FY26 sales compounded at about 17% a year [E] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: The consensus framing, a smart-meter-enclosure maker riding RDSS, is out of date [AI]. Per the annual report, about three-quarters of FY26 revenue came from EPC, and half came from solar EPC booked through subsidiaries that buy goods from the parent [F] (AR2026 p.27; AR2026 p.61). Our view is that the market is right to apply a very large discount but for a different reason than growth [AI]. The reverse DCF's -11.4% implied CAGR [F] (NUMBERS) is a cash-conversion and credibility discount, not a demand call. The equity re-rates only if FY27 shows positive operating cash flow, falling receivable ageing and a rights issue that does not transfer value away from minorities [AI]. Absent that, cheap headline multiples can persist or worsen through dilution [AI].

blocks.text: The Rs 208.99 cr of subsidiary turnover in AOC-1 roughly equals the Rs 208.99 cr solar EPC vertical [E] (AR2026 p.37; AR2026 p.6). Solar EPC is therefore effectively a subsidiary business [AI]. The parent bought out Ashok Agarwal's shares in RMC Solar Park during FY26 (Rs 2.70 lakh) [F] (AR2026 p.83), and directors hold small direct stakes in RMC Green Energy [F] (AR2026 p.96).

The Rs 400 cr business is about two years old [AI]. Electrical EPC became material only in FY24-FY25. Solar EPC went from Rs 1.74 cr to Rs 208.99 cr in one year through entities incorporated from mid-2024 [F] (AR2026 p.27; AR2026 p.31). The legacy enclosure franchise, which built the utility pre-qualifications, was Rs 60.84 cr of revenue in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.27). Revenue was Rs 132 cr in FY19 and Rs 41.6 cr in FY22 [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.7). Nothing in the folder explains the FY19-FY22 collapse; it is not disclosed. The 30-year history therefore says little about the economics of the current revenue mix [AI].

subsections.title: Production and service chain, step by step

items: Step 1, pre-qualification: credentials with more than twenty state utilities and gencos gate access to tenders [MC] (AR2026 p.13).
Step 2, bidding: tender pipeline above Rs 1,500 cr with historical conversion of about 30-35% [MC] (AR2026 p.14).

Step 3, materials: copper, aluminium, electrical-grade steel and polymers; modules and mounting structures for solar [F] (AR2026 p.14). In-house SMC compounding, moulding, pultrusion, metal fabrication and tool room [F] (AR2026 p.10).
Step 4, manufacture or procure: products made at Chaksu; solar inputs bought in. The parent bought Rs 115.35 cr of stock-in-trade in FY26 against nil in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.56).
Step 5, site execution: survey, installation and commissioning. Revenue on works contracts is recognised over time on a cost-to-cost basis [F] (AR2026 p.47).

Step 6, billing and collection: bills become payable only after utility acceptance, and there is 'no due date concept in government' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). About 10% retention is released after completion [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Stated credit terms are 120-150 days [F] (AR2026 p.50).

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and why

blocks.text: Management's indicative margins are about 9% for Electrical Products, 18% for Electrical EPC and 17% for Solar EPC [MC] (PPT Sep 2026). On those numbers the 'manufacturing core' earns the least, which contradicts the narrative that certified products 'lift blended margins' [AI]. The company says gross profit stayed flat at Rs 95.06 cr while revenue rose Rs 83.86 cr [F] (AR2026 p.9). Incremental EPC revenue therefore added volume and working capital but no gross profit [AI]. Value is captured in bid pricing and procurement timing, not in proprietary content, and fixed-price contracts without escalation pushed input inflation onto RMC [MC] (AR2026 p.8).

Fixed capital is light: FY26 fixed-asset turnover was 7.18x and capex/sales 5.5% [F] (NUMBERS). Working capital is heavy: receivables were 55.9% of consolidated assets [E] (AR2026 p.67). Job-work charges of Rs 5.38 cr [F] (AR2026 p.57) and purchased stock-in-trade show reliance on outsourced inputs [AI]. Our classification is asset-light in fixed assets and capital-heavy in working capital, which is the profile where reported ROCE overstates cash returns [AI].

blocks.text: Enclosures, feeder pillars, panels and both EPC lines are commodity-like: they are tendered on price after pre-qualification [AI]. The CEO calls the EPC business a 'red ocean market... where the price decides everything' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). items: Electrical EPC (-62%): management cites extended Maharashtra rainfall and procurement problems that delayed execution [MC] (AR2026 p.27). Our read: FY25 was inflated by the MSEDCL Jalna/Satara project, which is now 'near completion' [F] (AR2026 p.17). Its replacement (JVVNL Rs 143.50 cr, RVPN Rs 70.02 cr, PGVCL Rs 333.80 cr) was won during or after FY26, so the gap is a lumpy order cycle, not just weather [AI].

Solar EPC (n.m.): management says large solar orders moved into execution [MC] (AR2026 p.27). Our read: the vertical runs through new subsidiaries and absorbed most of the input-cost shock, with orders 'cancelled, reworked or deferred' [F] (AR2026 p.28). The year-end solar book was only about Rs 125 cr [MC] (AR2026 p.28). We expect solar revenue to fall sharply in FY27, consistent with the Q1 commentary that Solar EPC 'contributed far less' [MC] (PPT Sep 2026) [AI].

Electrical Products (+59%): management cites RDSS metering demand [MC] (AR2026 p.27). Our read: this is the most organic line, but some of it may be captive supply into own EPC projects; inter-vertical eliminations are not disclosed [AI].

blocks.text: Electrical EPC and Solar EPC are order-driven and lumpy: 76% of FY26 revenue [F] (AR2026 p.6). subsections.title: Mix change, currency, tariffs and trade policy

items: Mix change: the move away from exports looks incidental to the scale of domestic EPC, not a strategy. Management says 'first help yourself, then help others' on overseas PulseBox [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) [AI].

Currency: imported raw materials were 0% of consumption in FY25 and FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.56). Yet management cites a ~9% rupee depreciation to about 93.4/USD raising landed input costs [MC] (AR2026 p.9). The exposure is indirect, through dollar-linked commodity and module prices, and the subsidiaries' imports are not disclosed [AI].

Trade policy: China-linked supply disruption and safeguard-duty movements hit solar input costs in FY26 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The DCR cell requirement from June 2026 drove the module-plant deferral [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The central government's hold on 42 GW of PPAs was raised as a demand risk; management says EPC was unaffected [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).
Single location: all manufacturing is at Chaksu, near Jaipur [F] (AR2026 p.10). A plant disruption would hit Electrical Products and captive EPC supply [AI].
